sentences.text: Aisha Rahman (S2) attended the meeting in her capacity as a client.
The meeting took place on Wednesday, the twenty-third of September.
Daniel Okafor (S1) is a solicitor in the employment team.
Sophie Grant (S3) will assist by taking copies of documents brought by Aisha Rahman (S2).
Aisha Rahman attended the meeting with Daniel Okafor (Solicitor) and Sophie Grant (Trainee) in her capacity as the client.
The meeting duration was approximately forty minutes (possibly less).
Harbour Freight parcel company interview scheduled for next Tuesday, Ln 218
Solicitor (S1) attended the meeting in their professional capacity.
Client (S2) attended the meeting in their personal capacity as the claimant.
The purpose of the meeting was to outline next steps, confirm timelines, and provide advice regarding the ongoing employment dispute.
Aisha Rahman (S2) started working for Northgate Logistics Limited on the fifth of March 2018.
Aisha Rahman (S2) worked as a picker for Northgate Logistics Limited before becoming a team leader.
Aisha Rahman (S2) became a team leader for inbound goods in June 2021.
Aisha Rahman (S2) managed an eleven-person team during her role as team leader.
Aisha Rahman (S2) worked full-time, with a shift pattern of seven to seven (quarter past seven) and four-on-four-off days.
Aisha Rahman (S2) reported her annual basic salary as £29,400 (with a shift allowance of approximately £1,800).
Aisha Rahman (S2) has type one diabetes since she was fourteen years old.
Aisha Rahman (S2) uses a glucose sensor and insulin injections to manage her diabetes.
Aisha Rahman (S2) needs to manage her diabetes based on immediate symptoms, such as dropping blood sugar levels, which requires immediate glucose intake (e.g., juice, glucose tabs)
Aisha Rahman (S2) informed Northgate Logistics Limited about her diabetes at the start of her employment.
Linda Chu (manager) was Aisha Rahman’s manager until the end of 2022, and she was supportive of Aisha Rahman’s diabetes management.
Linda Chu (C-H-U) left Northgate Logistics Limited at the end of 2022.
Gary Whitlock (operations manager) is the new manager for the inbound side, starting on the twelfth of January 2023.
Gary Whitlock implemented a policy requiring fixed break times (30 minutes and two 15-minute breaks) and mandatory supervisor approval for leaving the dock outside those times.
Aisha Rahman (S2) had no formal written agreement regarding stepping off for diabetes management with Linda Chu.
Aisha Rahman (S2) had an informal arrangement with Linda Chu to step off for short breaks when managing her diabetes, which was not documented.
Aisha Rahman (S2) had a quarterly team leadership certificate from 2023, which she believes is in the kitchen drawer.
Aisha Rahman (S2) has the original contract from 2018 but no copy of the updated contract when she became team leader.
Aisha Rahman (S2) described concerns about dropping unexpectedly due to her condition, comparing it to needing the toilet.
Aisha Rahman (S2) did not put anything in writing to Gary Rahman (S2’s manager) at the time of initial concerns.
Aisha Rahman (S2) emailed HR in March to request an occupational health (OH) referral, citing uncertainty about Gary’s reaction to her condition.
The OH referral was granted, and she had a phone appointment with a nurse.
The OH report was issued on **22 April** and stated she should be allowed short breaks for testing and eating as a reasonable adjustment.
Aisha Rahman (S2) does not have a physical copy of the OH report but believes HR sent it to her personal email.
Aisha Rahman (S2) requested HR send the OH report to her personal email, which they did.
After the OH report, Gary Rahman (S2’s manager) said he would ‘take it on board’ but did not follow up formally.
Aisha Rahman (S2) had a ‘conversation’ with Gary on **19 May** regarding her team observing her leaving the dock.
Gary did not issue a formal warning or letter during the May conversation; it was described as informal.
Aisha Rahman (S2) has never received a verbal or written warning in her **eight years** at the company.
Aisha Rahman (S2) confirmed no written records of being late exist in any letters or files.
Aisha Rahman (S2) stated she had never been late but suspected it might be mentioned hypothetically.
Aisha Rahman (S2) left the dock on **1 July** and **3 July**, stepping off for **10–12 minutes** each time.
Aisha Rahman (S2) stepped off the dock on **9 July** due to severe symptoms (sensor reading **2.1**), leading to a **4.5-hour unpaid absence**.
Gary Rahman (S2’s manager) sent Aisha Rahman home on **9 July**, stating she was ‘not fit to be there’.
Aisha Rahman (S2) lost **4.5 hours** of pay on the **9 July** shift, as she was not paid for the time she stepped off.
Marcus Bell (a first aider) documented Aisha Rahman’s symptoms via a photo of her phone sensor reading (**2.1**) on **9 July**.
Aisha Rahman (S2) attended an **investigation meeting on 17 July** with Dean Farrow (shift manager), discussing her three absences.
Dean Farrow recorded Aisha Rahman’s reasons for stepping off the dock in the investigation meeting, referencing the OH report.
Aisha Rahman (S2) did not receive a copy of the notes from the **17 July** investigation meeting.
Aisha Rahman (S2) received a disciplinary letter on **28 July**, alleging unauthorised absence and failure to follow a reasonable management instruction, with a possible outcome of
The disciplinary letter on **28 July** stated a possible outcome was **dismissal**.
Aisha Rahman (S2) attended the disciplinary meeting on **6 August** with Gary Rahman (manager) and HR representative Kerry Doyle.
Gary Rahman chaired the disciplinary meeting on **6 August** and noted Aisha Rahman’s condition was documented in the OH report.
Gary Rahman stated the OH report said ‘where operationally possible’ regarding reasonable adjustments.
Aisha Rahman (S2) argued she could not radio Gary on **9 July** due to severe symptoms, and she had radioed on the other days.
Tomasz Nowak (Aisha Rahman’s unofficial deputy) accompanied her to the disciplinary meeting on **6 August** but was reportedly scared.
The disciplinary meeting occurred without Aisha Rahman’s presence; she was not present and did not see the notes.
Aisha Rahman received a disciplinary outcome letter dated **14 August 2026**, stating her employment would terminate with effect from that date.
The disciplinary outcome letter was received via email at **~5:00 PM on 14 August 2026** and by post on **Saturday (unspecified date, likely 15 August 2026)**.
The letter stated Aisha’s employment was terminated for **repeated failure to follow reasonable management instructions** (misconduct, not gross misconduct).
Aisha Rahman received **£4,523** in lieu of notice (eight weeks' pay).
The payment was credited to her bank account via the final pay at the end of August 2026.
Aisha Rahman believes she had **six days of accrued holiday** but is unsure if it was paid out.
The disciplinary letter did not mention Aisha’s **diabetes** or the **occupational health (OH) report**.
Aisha Rahman’s appeal was lodged via email on **19 August 2026** to HR, copied to Kerry.
The appeal was heard by **Claire Ashdown** on **2 September 2026** via Teams (with technical difficulties).
The appeal outcome letter was sent on **16 September 2026**, upholding dismissal.
Claire Ashdown addressed Aisha’s appeal points as follows: (1) Gary was deemed the best person to hear the case due to his knowledge of the facts; (2) Fixed breaks (an adjustment)
She claimed Aisha did not use fixed breaks properly.
During the appeal, Kerry (HR) suggested Aisha could accept a settlement if she wanted to go quietly, but did not specify terms or amount.
Aisha Rahman did not receive any **settlement agreement, document to sign, or formal acknowledgment letter** after the appeal.
Aisha Rahman heard from a colleague, **Jodie**, that Gary called her a
Jodie heard the remark from someone else in a managers' meeting on **Monday (unspecified date)**.
Jodie did not attend the meeting herself; the remark was second-hand (possibly third-hand).
Aisha Rahman has **not signed anything** without consulting the solicitor.

Aisha Rahman (S2) wants to understand her rights regarding diabetes management and break times at work.
Aisha Rahman has not worked since **14 August 2026**, but has applied for **15+ jobs** (mostly warehouse supervisor/team leader roles).
S2 plans to book an appointment with their GP if they can get through on the phone, Ln 231-232

Solicitor Daniel Okafor (S1) advised that the meeting would take approximately forty-five minutes, and the parking issue would not delay the session.
Solicitor Daniel Okafor (S1) confirmed that everything said by Aisha Rahman (S2) would be kept confidential.
Solicitor Daniel Okafor (S1) suggested that Aisha Rahman (S2) provide payslips for confirmation of her salary details.
Solicitor (S1) advised finding the OH report as the most critical document after letters.
Daniel Okafor advised Aisha to request a **Data Subject Access Request (DSAR)** to Northgate for her personnel file, disciplinary notes, emails, break policy, first aid log, and C
CCTV evidence may be limited to **30 days** and is likely expired, but worth requesting.
Daniel Okafor advised Aisha to **not sign any settlement agreement** without consulting the solicitor.

S1 notes that some recommendations may be more achievable through negotiated outcomes, Ln 237

S2 should not respond directly to Northgate’s correspondence; instead, send any letters to S1 for review before replying.
If Northgate sends a letter or offer, S2 should not sign it without consulting S1 first.
S2 should respond to inquiries about their departure from the job with a factual, brief statement: ‘It’s subject to an ongoing process, and I’d rather not go into detail.’
Aisha Rahman (S2) requested Sophie Grant (trainee) copy the disciplinary letter from **28 July** for further review.
Sophie Grant (Trainee) will take copies of Aisha’s documents for the file.
By Friday, October 25th, S2 must email S1 the Occupational Health (OH) report, Marcus’s photo of the sensor, any payslips not brought today, and the February email if available.
S2’s husband will check with Castleford Mutual for legal expenses cover by Monday, October 28th, and send S1 the policy schedule and wording.
By Friday, October 2nd, S2 must draft a timeline of events in their own words, including dates and details from today’s conversation.
S2 must keep a spreadsheet tracking every job application.
Trainee (Sophie Grant, S3) will draft a subject access request to Northgate by Monday, October 28th, and send it to both HR and the registered office.
S2 should ask Marcus if he would be willing to provide a statement, without going into detail.
S2 should ask Linda if she would be willing to talk to S1 at some point (no urgency).
S2 must meet with S1 on Thursday, October 8th, at 10:00 AM to discuss documents and ACAS notification (aimed for October 16th).
